source_user: Calculation case 78: a model has 40 layers, 4 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 1024, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 40 × 1024 × 4 × 128 × 2 = 83886080 bytes = 0.078125 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substitution: 2 x 40 x 1024 x 4 x 128 x 2 = 83886080 bytes = 80.000000 MiB = 0.078125 GiB.
Per-token cost (the number that actually governs admission control): 2 x 40 x 4 x 128 x 2 = 81920 bytes/token = 80.0000 KiB/token, so a 1024-token request costs 0.078125 GiB.
Mechanism: with GQA/MQA the KV cache scales with kv_heads (4), not query heads; dtype is BF16/FP16 at 2 byte(s) per value.
Boundary conditions this estimate does NOT cover: (1) paged-attention block granularity (e.g. vLLM block_size 16) rounds each sequence up to a whole number of blocks, adding up to block_size-1 tokens of internal fragmentation per sequence; (2) INT8/FP8 KV quantization needs per-block scales/zero-points (typically +1-3% overhead) which are excluded here; (3) prefix/radix cache sharing can make the marginal cost of a request far lower than this number; (4) allocator metadata, CUDA context, weights, activation and CUDA-graph pools are excluded; (5) speculative decoding or beam search multiplies live KV by the number of candidate branches.
Falsifiable prediction: on an A30 (24 GiB) serving stack, setting gpu_memory_utilization so that free KV bytes = N x 83886080 should admit approximately N concurrent 1024-token sequences, +/-1 block of rounding per sequence.
Evidence required before trusting this in capacity planning: vLLM startup log line reporting '# GPU blocks' and KV cache size; torch.cuda.memory_summary() or nvidia-smi steady-state used memory under a fixed concurrency; a load test that raises concurrency until preemption/recompute counters appear in the server metrics.
Rollback threshold: if measured KV bytes/token exceed this analytic value by >10%, or if preemption/swap counters become non-zero at the planned concurrency, reduce max_num_seqs or max_model_len and re-measure before rolling the config to production.
risks: Source answer omits paged-attention block rounding, so real allocation is >= the stated value.
Per-token KV cost is not stated, which is the quantity needed for admission control and max_num_seqs sizing.
BF16/FP16 assumption must be confirmed against the served checkpoint dtype and any KV-quant flags.
Using a single-request figure for cluster capacity planning ignores fragmentation, prefix sharing and preemption.

Boundary conditions this estimate does NOT cover: (1) paged-attention block granularity (e.g. vLLM block_size 16) rounds each sequence up to a whole number of blocks, adding up to block_size-1 tokens of internal fragmentation per sequence; (2) INT8/FP8 KV quantization needs per-block scales/zero-points (typically +1-3% overhead) which are excluded here; (3) prefix/radix cache sharing can make the marginal cost of a request far lower than this number; (4) allocator metadata, CUDA context, weights, activation and CUDA-graph pools are excluded; (5) speculative decoding or beam search multiplies live KV by the number of candidate branches.
Falsifiable prediction: on an A30 (24 GiB) serving stack, setting gpu_memory_utilization so that free KV bytes = N x 113246208 should admit approximately N concurrent 3072-token sequences, +/-1 block of rounding per sequence.
Evidence required before trusting this in capacity planning: vLLM startup log line reporting '# GPU blocks' and KV cache size; torch.cuda.memory_summary() or nvidia-smi steady-state used memory under a fixed concurrency; a load test that raises concurrency until preemption/recompute counters appear in the server metrics.
Rollback threshold: if measured KV bytes/token exceed this analytic value by >10%, or if preemption/swap counters become non-zero at the planned concurrency, reduce max_num_seqs or max_model_len and re-measure before rolling the config to production.
risks: Source answer omits paged-attention block rounding, so real allocation is >= the stated value.
Per-token KV cost is not stated, which is the quantity needed for admission control and max_num_seqs sizing.
BF16/FP16 assumption must be confirmed against the served checkpoint dtype and any KV-quant flags.
Using a single-request figure for cluster capacity planning ignores fragmentation, prefix sharing and preemption.
